ogTitle: Top 10 Popular Restaurants in Rayong — Seafood at Pak Nam, Local Food, and Beachside Cafés That People Talk About Most
ogDesc: Our top 10 popular restaurants in Rayong — original seafood legends, local heritage food, ho mok, fish wontons, and a beachside café. Honest, with signature dishes and prices.
eyebrow: Where to Eat in Rayong · Popular Restaurants
intro: Rayong is a coastal city where great food hides around every corner — search once and you'll find hundreds of places with no idea where to start. We've pulled together the 10 restaurants locals and visitors talk about most, from legendary seafood at Pak Nam and heritage home cooking in the old town to beachside cafés and regional specialities like ho mok and fish wontons. Every restaurant on this list is genuinely open and backed by real reviews. We tell it straight — both the highlights and the things worth knowing before you go.
chips: 🏛️ Local food from the old town

blocks.html:
If you want an Eastern Gulf coast city where you can eat fresh seafood all day without ever getting bored, Rayong belongs at the top of the list. This is home to large sea bass, blue crabs and prawns that came off the boats this morning, and tropical fruits like durian and pineapple that get worked into punchy local cooking. Walk the old town along Yomchinda Road and soak in the wooden shophouses and the old governor's residence, then move on to seafood by the shore at Mae Ramphung Beach, or drive out all the way to Ban Phe and the Klaeng coast where beachside cafés sit with the sea breeze coming through. The charm of Rayong is that it has both decades-old institutions that have been part of the city for generations and newer atmospheric spots to choose between depending on your mood. If you love fresh seafood and honest local cooking, Rayong delivers every single meal.

This list has all the Rayong legends in one place. It opens with Laem Charoen Seafood original branch at Pak Nam — the place that started as a tiny shed in 1979 and became the first to make the now-iconic fish-sauce-fried sea bass, growing into a chain of more than thirty branches nationwide. Then Krua Khru Mu in the old wooden Yomchinda family house by the river, which still keeps Rayong curry and old-style glass noodle stir-fry recipes intact. For beachside seafood, there's both Jae Ueng and Jae Yindee at Mae Ramphung Beach. For the regional specialities you don't want to miss: Ho Mok Pa Jiw at Ban Phe and Kiao Pla Nai Khiam Original in Klaeng. For a full slow day by the sea, She Sails Café & Beach Club has a fire show every Saturday night. Work through the list and your Rayong trip will be good from the first meal to the last.

blocks.name: Laem Charoen Seafood (Original Branch, Rayong Pak Nam)
blocks.signature: Fish-sauce-fried sea bass, crab fried rice, prawns marinated in fish sauce
blocks.descHtml:
When people in Rayong talk about seafood, Laem Charoen Seafood is almost always the first name on their lips — and the original branch at Pak Nam Rayong is where it all began. The restaurant has been open since 1979, starting from a tiny waterside shed, and today it's a brand with branches across Bangkok's shopping malls and more. But regular visitors and Rayong locals will tell you that if you want the original atmosphere and the real thing, this riverside branch is the place to come. A natural choice for families or groups who want fresh seafood by the water with a sea breeze coming through.

The dish that made the restaurant famous — and the one every table orders — is the fish-sauce-fried sea bass: crispy skin on the outside, soft sweet flesh inside, dressed with the restaurant's own fish sauce recipe that balances sweet, salty, and savoury perfectly alongside a bowl of hot steamed rice. Follow that with the crab fried rice, fragrant and loose, loaded with crab meat, and the prawns marinated in fish sauce — fresh plump prawns, springy flesh, dipped in the restaurant's signature spicy seafood sauce. For heat lovers, the pohtak tom yum or sour curry are both described in reviews as bold and punchy.

Prices sit at the mid-to-slightly-higher end — around 250–500 THB per person when you order a spread. A large fried sea bass runs around 460–490 THB, which is fair for the quality and generous portion size. The setting is an open breezy space by the water; behind the restaurant is a fishing harbour, and in the evening you can walk over to photograph the view. Plenty of seating, comfortable for large tables.

Open every day 10:00–21:30, on the coastal road at Pak Nam Rayong — easy to drive to. Key thing to know: on long weekends and Saturday–Sunday it gets very busy, parking can be tight, and there may be a wait. Coming before noon or in the late afternoon is usually more relaxed. Google reviews sit at around 4.3 stars from several thousand reviewers — a restaurant that people genuinely return to.
blocks.bestFor: Families and groups for seafood by the sea
blocks.spice: Bold options (tom yum / sour curry) and mild dishes both available

blocks.name: Krua Khru Mu (Yomchinda Family Original)
blocks.area: Yomchinda Road, Tambon Tha Pradoo, Mueang Rayong District, Rayong
blocks.signature: Rayong curry, garlic-pickle omelette, old-style glass noodle stir-fry
blocks.descHtml:
Krua Khru Mu is a Rayong heritage home-cooking restaurant in an old wooden riverside house on Yomchinda Road in the old town. The building is a century-old wooden residence of the Yomchinda family — descendants of an old governor of Rayong. The owner is Khru Mu, a former home economics teacher who took family recipes and opened a restaurant. It's the perfect choice for anyone who wants real Rayong home cooking, and for walking around the old timber-and-antique-filled rooms at the same time. Less like eating at a restaurant, more like eating at a relative's house.

The most talked-about dish is Rayong curry — a thick, spicy, sour gravy with pineapple chunks, bold with fresh herbs from an old recipe. Almost every table also orders the old-style glass noodle stir-fry: a slightly sweet, silky texture that works for anyone who doesn't take spice. The garlic-pickle omelette (old-style omelette) has a fragrant pickled-garlic note that cuts through richness beautifully — not to be missed as part of the full spread. For larger groups, adding the milky fish tom yum and fried rice with salted egg rounds out a proper Rayong-style set.

The atmosphere is as much a draw as the food — sitting in an old wooden house by the river, surrounded by artefacts that tell the story of Rayong, with a cool breeze flowing through. Most reviews praise the rare local flavours and the warm feel of the place. Prices are kind at about 120–180 THB per person. Wongnai rates it around 4.0 stars; Tripadvisor from international visitors gives around 4.2 — a restaurant both locals and travellers talk about.

Worth knowing: the restaurant is open evenings only, 17:00–21:00 daily. Food is cooked fresh to order so expect to wait a little, especially on busy evenings. If you're coming as a group, calling ahead to book is wise — seating in the wooden house is limited. Once you arrive, don't rush out — walk around the old governor's residence and its collection of artefacts for the full experience.
blocks.bestFor: A dinner of authentic Rayong food in an old riverside house

blocks.name: Jae Ueng Seafood Mae Ramphung Beach
blocks.area: Mae Ramphung Beach, Mueang Rayong District, Rayong
blocks.signature: Prawn cakes, tamarind prawns, crab fried rice, blue crab som tam
blocks.descHtml:
Jae Ueng Seafood has been open for over 20 years at Mae Ramphung Beach, and it has become a name that locals and tourists reach for when they want really fresh seafood sitting with the sound of waves. The standout feature of the place is the fresh ingredients displayed in trays right at the front of the restaurant — prawns, shellfish, crabs, fish — as if the sea itself were laid out for you to pick through. Choose what you want, decide how it's prepared, and they cook it. A natural choice for families or groups who want proper seafood without paying above the odds.

The dishes that come up in reviews most often are the prawn cakes — firm and springy, dense prawn filling; tamarind prawns, pleasantly sour-sweet and well-rounded; crab fried rice, fragrant and packed with crab meat; and blue crab som tam, fiery and satisfying. Another dish reviewers consistently praise is the fish-sauce-fried sea bass — fresh fish, crispy outside, soft inside, with the restaurant's house seafood sauce punched up with fresh lime. The consensus across reviews: genuinely fresh ingredients, generous size, and an outstanding dipping sauce that makes everything land.

Two seating options: comfortable indoor seating, or tables outside by the beach under the shade with a sea breeze. The evening before sunset is the best time for atmosphere. Price per person around 250–500 THB — good value for beachside seafood. Parking available.

Located on the Mae Ramphung Beach road, Ratchaburi Road RY.1001, Tambon Tapong, Mueang Rayong. Open every day 09:00–21:00. Key note: on long weekends it gets very busy — if you're coming as a large group, calling ahead to book is more comfortable. Check seafood prices by weight before ordering to gauge your budget accurately.
blocks.bestFor: A group seafood meal by the beach with a cool breeze

blocks.name: Nai Don Makham Thao 2539
blocks.signature: Tom klong mixed seafood (tom yum style), pomelo salad, red curry with roast duck
blocks.descHtml:
Nai Don Makham Thao 2539 is a Rayong institution that grew from a legendary street-cart rice soup stall into a proper sit-down restaurant that has been part of the city for nearly thirty years. If you're in Rayong and want bold Eastern Thai home cooking the way local people actually eat it, this is the answer. A good fit for families, groups of friends, or anyone looking for a warm, laid-back evening meal with plenty of flavour. The restaurant has earned the Thai Select 2020 mark — a recognition for genuine Thai food cooked with consistent quality.

The must-order is the tom klong mixed seafood — called 'tom jo' at this restaurant — a tom yum-style broth that's sour, spicy, and salty, packed with mixed seafood and a deeply layered stock. It's the house signature and the first thing most tables order. Another dish that gets talked about constantly is the Nai Don pomelo salad — a well-balanced sweet-sour dressing with peeled pomelo segments, shredded pork, and prawns; multiple real reviews say 'really love this dish.' The red curry with roast duck is another star: thick, smooth curry sauce, tender duck, a natural partner for steamed rice. For something more local, try the Rayong shrimp-paste ho lon or stir-fried bai liang with egg.

Prices are excellent value — dishes start around 80–90 THB, the pomelo salad is 99 THB, the duck curry is 129 THB, and the large tom jo runs around 185–250 THB. Two people can eat a filling meal for around 400 THB. The general verdict from reviewers: 'delicious and cheap,' generous portions for the price. The restaurant's reputation for consistency and fast service across generations is what keeps people coming back.

Located on Khlong Khut Soi, behind the Rayong Post Office, Mueang Rayong. Open daily ~11:00–23:00 (best in evenings). Parking available but a little tight; staff help direct. The entrance is down a small lane — opening Google Maps to the pin coordinates is the easiest way to find it.
blocks.bestFor: Evening meal with family or friends; bold regional Thai food
blocks.spice: Medium–spicy (tom jo / salad dishes are bold; adjustable)

blocks.name: She Sails Cafe & Beach Club
blocks.area: Tambon Chak Phong, Klaeng District, Rayong
blocks.cuisine: Café & Beach Club (Thai–Western, seafood, drinks / cocktails)
blocks.signature: Drinks / coffee by the sea, food, cocktails (fire show every Saturday)
blocks.descHtml:
If you're exploring Rayong around Klaeng District and want a beachside café where you can sit all day from morning to late night, She Sails Café & Beach Club is the one most people mention first. The café is in Tambon Chak Phong, designed in a Balinese–beach-club style, with a large casuarina tree — the provincial tree — as the centrepiece of the setting. Walk straight down to the beach, look out over several islands including Ko Thalu and Ko Samet lined up on the horizon. A natural fit for couples, groups, or families who want a slow, easy day by the sea without rushing.

Dishes that reviewers mention most often are the fish and chips — large fresh fish, a thin crispy batter — and the She Sails Snack, which takes local Rayong seafood and puts it into a shareable plate. For main meals there are BBQ Pork Ribs and Spaghetti Truffle Scallops with ikura to try. On the coffee side the beans are Colombian; the latte is fragrant and not too sweet. Non-coffee drinkers can try the matcha yuzu or iced matcha latte, which works perfectly in the sea-breeze heat. Later in the evening there are mocktails and cocktails for lingering.

Real reviews generally say the food is good overall, the prawns are large and fresh, and the pasta is rich and satisfying. Staff are attentive and the atmosphere is a clear winner across the board. Multiple seating zones are available: bar zone, camper-van zone, beach zone — every corner is photogenic. Per-person spend around 251–500 THB, fair for a beachside venue.

What makes this place pop: every Saturday there's a fire show at around 20:30, plus a happy hour on drinks from 16:00–19:00. Open every day 09:00–23:00 daily (Fire show Sat ~20:30, Happy Hour 16:00–19:00). Pets welcome, parking available. Note: being right by the sea means there may be insects in the evening, and weekends are busy. If you're coming as a group or want a good spot, coming mid-morning or checking ahead is worth it.
blocks.bestFor: Couples or groups for a slow day by the sea from morning to late

blocks.name: Kiao Pla Nai Khiam (Original)
blocks.signature: Fish wonton (wonton skin made from pure sea fish), three-flavour wonton, mixed noodle soup
blocks.descHtml:
If you're passing through Klaeng and want something that's genuinely a local speciality, Kiao Pla Nai Khiam Original in the Sam Yan Market area is the first name anyone in Rayong will give you. The restaurant has been part of Klaeng city for over 60 years, passed down from the grandfather's generation. What makes it different from every other wonton shop is the wonton skin: made from real sea fish flesh, no flour added. Once it's blanched the skin is thin, translucent, springy and chewy — nothing like the flour-based wonton skins you find elsewhere. An ideal first meal of the trip if you're driving through, or a proper stop for anyone who loves good handmade noodles.

The must-order is the fish wonton itself — firm sea fish filling, thin see-through skin — and the three-flavour wonton, dressed with a balanced sour-sweet-salty sauce. If you're in a larger group, the mixed noodle soup (small noodles with everything) is the best way to go: fish wontons, three-flavour wontons, jade wontons, fish balls, all in one bowl. Reviews consistently say the broth is gently sweet and full-flavoured, the fish noodles are chewy and never go soft, and the bowl is large value for the price. Many people say 'every time I drive through Klaeng I have to stop.'

Prices are genuinely affordable — most items under 100 THB per bowl; mixed small noodles start at around 50 THB, special at 70 THB. The setting is an old-school open house, no air conditioning, but there's plenty of indoor and outdoor parking for large groups. Located on Thetsaban 2 Road, Tambon Thang Kwian, in the Sam Yan Old Market area. Open every day around 08:30–15:30.

The restaurant stays famous because it has kept the traditional fish-skin wonton recipe intact, along with the value and the word-of-mouth reputation built over decades — now a local signature and a Klaeng staple. Important: cash only, no transfers. Bring small bills. Holiday periods get busy — mid-morning or early afternoon is the most comfortable time to visit.
mustOrder: Fish wonton (pure sea fish wonton skin)
blocks.bestFor: First meal in the province / a proper stop for Klaeng's best local food

blocks.name: Krua Baan Baan by Jamlong
blocks.signature: Two-hearts sea bass, steamed seafood egg hot pot, crispy-fried sea bass with chilli sauce, raeng jwan curry
blocks.descHtml:
If you love seafood cooked with real skill and want to eat in a laid-back garden setting, Krua Baan Baan by Jamlong is one of the first names Rayong residents reach for. The owner is Jamlong, a former MasterChef Thailand Season 1 contestant who came back to open his own restaurant in the Thap Ma / Noen Phra area, set beside a prawn-fishing pond. Walk in and you'll find scattered garden tables under trees, a breeze coming through, no dress code required. Perfect for families and groups who want to sit and eat long and talk freely.

The dish customers talk about most is the 'two-hearts sea bass' — one whole sea bass prepared two ways on the same plate: half as larb (minced fish salad), half as crispy deep-fried cubes. Two flavours and textures from a single fish. The other dish that draws consistent praise is the 'steamed seafood egg hot pot' — silky soft egg, dense seafood, in a hot clay pot. Spice lovers should order the 'crispy-fried sea bass with chilli sauce' and the 'raeng jwan curry', both bold and deeply seasoned. For fresh raw seafood, the 'wasabi seafood yam' — springy fresh prawns and squid in a punchy wasabi dressing — is the one to add.

The overall consensus from reviews: food is excellent, consistent with a MasterChef pedigree — well-seasoned and fresh ingredients. Price per person around 251–500 THB — fair for the quality and quantity. On some evenings there's live music playing softly in the garden. Certain days can get busy, so leave yourself a little extra time.

Note: the restaurant is open-air, no air conditioning, fans only — midday in summer can be warm, but evenings have a great cool breeze. Ample parking. Open every day 10:30–22:00. For seafood cooked by a real chef in a garden atmosphere, this is a genuinely rewarding stop in Rayong.
mustOrder: Crispy-fried sea bass with chilli sauce
blocks.bestFor: An evening meal with family or friends; chef-cooked seafood in a garden
blocks.spice: Medium–spicy (yam and chilli stir-fry dishes are fiery)

blocks.name: Pa Tum Kuay Teow Kaeng Som
blocks.signature: Sour-curry noodle soup with acacia omelette, rice and curry, rice noodles with crab sauce
blocks.descHtml:
If you're driving through Ban Chang and get hungry, Pa Tum Kuay Teow Kaeng Som is the restaurant locals will point to first. It's a simple neighbourhood spot that's been open long enough to become a regular for everyone in the area — and it has earned multiple consecutive Wongnai Users' Choice awards. The star of the menu is the 'sour-curry noodle soup with acacia omelette': thick, concentrated sour-curry broth poured over noodles with a crispy acacia omelette on top. The flavour is sour-forward, then salty and sweet in layers — reviewers consistently agree that the broth needs no extra seasoning straight from the kitchen. The acacia omelette adds just the right crisp contrast. A perfect choice for anyone who wants to try something genuinely different from a standard noodle bowl.

Beyond the headline dish, the menu is wide enough to keep a table busy: multiple rice-and-curry plates that reviewers say are just as good as the noodles; rice noodles with crab sauce; som tam; fried chicken; and fruit som tam that many regulars can't shake. Prices start at 40–50 THB per dish — you can eat a full meal for well under 100 THB per person. One particular highlight reviewers flag is the dessert buffet corner: scoop as much as you like at a flat charge in the double-digits, making an already-good-value meal even better.

The setting is a Thai wooden house, airy and open, next to the public library with wide easy parking — great for families or a stop along the way. Open from morning through the afternoon, approximately 07:30–15:00. It's a busy, popular spot — on peak days some items sell out. Coming in the mid-morning gives you the fullest menu selection.

In short: Pa Tum sells real flavour, not just an unusual dish name. For anyone passing through Ban Chang–Samnak Thon who wants something delicious, generous, and genuinely local at a local price, this is the stop. Lead with the sour-curry acacia-omelette noodle, follow with rice-and-curry and crab rice noodles — you won't be disappointed.
mustOrder: Sour-curry noodle soup with acacia omelette
blocks.bestFor: Morning or lunch; families; a stop along the way

blocks.name: Jae Yindee Seafood
blocks.area: Mae Ramphung Beach, Mueang Rayong District, Rayong
blocks.signature: Grilled seafood, fish-sauce-fried sea bass, three-flavour fish with fresh chillies, squid stir-fried with salted egg
blocks.descHtml:
Jae Yindee Seafood is a veteran seafood restaurant right on Mae Ramphung Beach that locals and visitors have marked as a destination for over 30 years. The family started fishing in 1982 and built it into a full restaurant in 1994. The thing that every review agrees on is the freshness: ingredients arrive directly from the Rayong sea every day, and you pick them from the display at the front of the restaurant yourself. A natural match for families, groups, or anyone who wants seafood right on the beach, not just in a city restaurant.

The must-orders are the grilled seafood — fresh prawns, shellfish, and squid, grilled hot and served with the restaurant's bold seafood sauce — and the fish-sauce-fried sea bass, the house crowd favourite: crispy skin, sweet tender flesh. The three-flavour fish with fresh chillies hits sour-sweet-spicy in balance, and the squid stir-fried with salted egg is rich and moreish, a dish reviewers say they keep ordering again. Regulars add the garlic-fried scallops and crispy-fried soft-shell crab with garlic and pepper. The overall verdict: genuinely fresh, skilled preparation, bold dipping sauces, and generous portions.

The atmosphere is the other selling point: tables reach all the way down to the beach, with a sea breeze, a view of the fishing pier extending into the water, and space for children to play on the sand. The best time to come is late afternoon when the sun softens. Per person around 251–500 THB — fair for beachside fresh seafood. English menu available, cold beer, parking.

Located on RY.1001 Mae Ramphung Beach Road, Tambon Tapong, Mueang Rayong — easy to spot near the fishing pier across from the Rayong aquatic breeding station. Open every day 09:00–21:00. Note: long weekends and Saturday–Sunday evenings get very busy and food may take longer — as a few reviews mention. Calling ahead to book a table by the water is worth it.
blocks.bestFor: An evening meal by the beach with family or friends
blocks.spice: Adjustable; both mild and bold dishes available

blocks.name: Ho Mok Pa Jiw Ban Phe
blocks.signature: Genuine kingfish ho mok (steamed / grilled), rice noodles with crab sauce, sweet squid in black ink broth
blocks.descHtml:
If you're driving down to Ban Phe to catch the ferry to Ko Samet and you catch the fragrant smell of grilled ho mok drifting from near the Ban Phe market (100 Pillars Market), you're in the right place. Ho Mok Pa Jiw Ban Phe is a legendary neighbourhood shop that has been selling here long enough to become one of Rayong's signature gifts and local delicacies — locals and tourists stop for it without fail. It's a basic shophouse setup with fans; Pa Jiw the owner still works the counter herself almost every day, warm and welcoming to every customer. A good fit for families, groups, or anyone who wants to take home a genuine Rayong souvenir.

The star is the genuine kingfish ho mok, made fresh every day — available steamed and grilled. Reviewers are unanimous: silky soft ho mok flesh, bold spiced curry paste in a proper Southern Thai style. Many say the grilled version has more fragrance because of the subtle smokiness from the charcoal. The other must-order is the rice noodles with crab sauce — a rich, rounded sauce; and the sweet squid in black ink broth — fresh, clean, and deeply flavoured. Fried-fish lovers can add the fish-sauce-fried kingfish and fish cakes on the side.

Prices are genuinely affordable — ho mok starts in the low tens of baht per piece; a sit-down meal comes to about 101–250 THB per person. The restaurant opens early at 06:00 through to approximately 17:00 daily (closed on the 1st and 16th of each month). If you're planning to visit on one of those days, call ahead to check. Roadside parking available near the Ban Phe 100 Pillars Market.

This restaurant has stayed famous and lasted because of consistent flavour and fresh local seafood from Ban Phe — covered by media and well-known figures over the years. For anyone passing through Ban Phe who wants an authentic, bold ho mok to eat in or take home, Pa Jiw's is the pin to mark on your map.
mustOrder: Sweet squid in black ink broth
blocks.bestFor: Buying ho mok as a gift / a morning meal on the way to the ferry to Ko Samet
blocks.hours: 06:00–17:00 daily (closed on the 1st and 16th of each month)

blocks.title: Know Before You Eat in Rayong

items.title: Getting Around — Grab Works in the City
items.text: Rayong's restaurants are spread out considerably — from Pak Nam and Mae Ramphung Beach to Ban Phe and Klaeng. Grab works within the city centre, but if you want to hit several spots outside town, renting a car or motorbike is far more practical.

items.title: Local Spots Work on Cash
items.text: Fish wonton stalls, noodle shops, and ho mok stalls mostly accept cash only. Keep small bills on you. Larger seafood restaurants and cafés like She Sails usually accept QR-code payments and cards.

items.title: Avoid Seafood Restaurants at Weekend Lunchtime
items.text: Famous beachside seafood restaurants at Mae Ramphung and Pak Nam are packed at midday on weekends. If you want a comfortable table and no wait, try a weekday evening or call ahead to book.

items.title: Tipping
items.text: No tipping culture at Thai local restaurants. If you had a great meal and want to leave something, rounding up or leaving your loose change is appreciated — but it's never expected or required.

items.title: Menus — English Varies
items.text: Large seafood restaurants and cafés that serve many tourists usually have illustrated menus or English options. Small local spots may have Thai-only menus — pointing at pictures or showing a translation app works fine.

items.title: Tell Them Your Spice Level
items.text: Many Rayong regional dishes are genuinely spicy and bold — Rayong curry, tom klong, and salad dishes all have heat. If you can't take spice, tell the restaurant 'phrik noi' (less spice) or 'mai sai phrik' (no chilli). Fried and stir-fried seafood is usually mild.

blocks.title: How to Plan Your Rayong Eating Day
blocks.html: If you're staying in the Mueang Rayong area, Laem Charoen Seafood at Pak Nam, Krua Khru Mu on Yomchinda Road, and Nai Don Makham Thao behind the post office are all convenient stops. Mae Ramphung beachside seafood at Jae Ueng and Jae Yindee is a short drive east. Krua Khru Mu opens evenings only (approximately 17:00–21:00), so keep that for dinner. Regional specialities like Ho Mok Pa Jiw and Kiao Pla Nai Khiam Original are in the Ban Phe and Klaeng zones, further from the city centre — build those into a route. For She Sails Café & Beach Club in Chak Phong, going on a Saturday evening is worth it for the fire show at around 20:30. You can combine She Sails and Kiao Pla Nai Khiam efficiently on the same route out to Klaeng to save driving time.

faq.q: Which restaurant is the most famous in Rayong?
faq.a: By reach and reputation, Laem Charoen Seafood original branch at Pak Nam Rayong stands out — the place that started as a tiny shed in 1979, invented the now-iconic fish-sauce-fried sea bass, and grew into a chain with over thirty branches nationwide. For regional home cooking, Krua Khru Mu in the old Yomchinda family wooden house is the restaurant both locals and tourists talk about the most. Every restaurant on this list is genuinely open and backed by real reviews.

faq.q: What are Rayong's signature local dishes?
faq.a: The most iconic is fresh seafood: fish-sauce-fried sea bass, prawns in fish sauce, prawn cakes, and crab fried rice — available at Laem Charoen, Jae Ueng, and Jae Yindee. Rayong also has rare heritage dishes like Rayong curry and old-style glass noodle stir-fry at Krua Khru Mu, genuine kingfish ho mok at Pa Jiw Ban Phe, real fish-flesh wonton at Nai Khiam in Klaeng, and the sour-curry acacia-omelette noodle at Pa Tum in Ban Chang. The full range of sea food and local cooking.

faq.q: What do these restaurants cost per person?
faq.a: Local noodle and bowl spots like Kiao Pla Nai Khiam and Pa Tum Kaeng Som start from a few dozen THB per bowl, averaging under 100 THB per person. Nai Don Makham Thao runs around 80–250 THB per dish. Sit-down seafood restaurants like Laem Charoen, Jae Ueng, Jae Yindee, and Krua Baan Baan — when ordering a spread to share — come out to around 250–500 THB per person. She Sails Café is around 251–500 THB per person.

faq.q: Do I need to book a table in advance?
faq.a: Local and small spots like Kiao Pla Nai Khiam, Pa Tum, and Ho Mok Pa Jiw are mostly walk-in — come early to avoid queues and sell-outs. Sit-down seafood restaurants like Laem Charoen and Krua Baan Baan get very busy on Saturday and Sunday; calling ahead to book is worth it. She Sails on Saturday evenings for the fire show also gets busy — checking hours with the restaurant page before heading out is always a good idea, since some places have set closing days.

faq.q: Which restaurants are open in the evening or late?
faq.a: Krua Khru Mu opens evenings only, around 17:00–21:00 — perfect for dinner. She Sails Café & Beach Club is open until 23:00 with a fire show every Saturday. Sit-down seafood restaurants like Laem Charoen, Jae Ueng, Jae Yindee, and Krua Baan Baan are all open through the evening. Regional local spots like Kiao Pla Nai Khiam, Pa Tum, and Ho Mok Pa Jiw sell during daytime through the afternoon and often sell out — check their hours and check in early.
